tips.comment: Good stable, in form 8-year-old, winning twice and placed 4 times in its last 6 runs. Last time out won over C/D, made all and ran on final 110 yards, beat Rebel Star. Goes for its 12th career win, still looks well treated, serious chance.
Merrimack's start at Newmarket two starts back should have this horse easily as favourite. The last start was disappointing, but backing this horse to bounce back here.
Broke his duck at the 18th time of asking when winning over 6 furlongs here in April. Fair efforts in a couple of starts since but is of interest back at this venue today.
Beaten by Pop Dancer last time out. Reopposes Pop Dancer today on favorable terms. Rebel Star has been in decent form since March. Looks overpriced at 8/1.

Finally broke his maiden at the 14th try with a strong win here over 6f. Has form at the track and handles the conditions well here. Drop to 5f isn’t a worry, and he looks on the up. Each-way claims here.

David Egan - 26.3% SR at Brighton last 12 months. Havana Grey at Brighton as a Sire - 1.17 A/E - 27% SR. £300k purchase. Neither Mission Complete or Dazzling Haze finished their maidens well, ranked 4th and 5th for the final furlong. Yard 1 winner and 5 places from 12 runners in 2YO races. Amo Racing 20% SR with 2YO Debutantes, 1.06 A/E - increases to 41.2% SR with horses that are SP Fav.

Dazzling Haze is a well-bred filly, purchased for £130,000, signaling high expectations from connections. Her debut third at Thirsk was promising??'beaten just 3¼ lengths in what looked a decent maiden, suggesting she has latent potential that’s likely to improve with race experience.

Could prove difficult to pass if Mission Classified can get on the front end and get an easy lead. 3rd at Goodwood in May and led for a long way before getting passed, but jockey Hollie Doyle might have a better idea of his ability today.

2-year-old maiden event. Did not get its run here last time out. 3 rivals that ran that day have been entered into class 4 and 2 events, including a rival who was behind that day.
Suggest this horse is better than odds claim it to be

Winner over today's course and distance last time out and looked to have plenty more to come that day. Raised six pounds for that effort, but with a favourable draw in stall three, can land the quick-fire double.

Tony Carroll has Time Patrol in very decent form at present and has won three races in a row at Brighton by the end of May. His handicap mark has now been raised 4 lbs, but the horse gives unrelenting effort and is delivered late in the race, making it difficult for the handicapper to stop him from winning. In his last run, Time Patrol had a bit to spare, so I have come to the conclusion that at 4/1, I will go each way just in case David Egan gets his effort a bit late. However, I do fully expect Time Patrol to win again.

Maybe better known as a Aw horse, but interesting that @ the age of 8 they are having their first run @ Brighton. Normally competes @ a higher level than this 5, very well treated in this class off today's dropping mark of 72, very good jockey who does well for this stable back up and very shrewd trainer 27 percent with his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 7.50 solid Ew value in the race.

Race 5 at Brighton today is a Handicap (Class 5) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,399 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old filly Bint Havana Gold from the Richard Hughes yard. She will be ridden by Finley Marsh, one of only 2 fillies in the race. This daughter of Havana Gold is a three-time winner, and if there was an award for consistency, she would get it hands down with 16 of her last 19 runs hitting seven 3rd placed finishes, five 2nd placed, and four winners. She gets on well with jockey Marsh and is distance suited. She has to be a major player today.

Has never been the most consistent and was terrible last time in follow-up bid, possibly the race coming too soon. Runs off 5lb higher mark here, but is well in on old form. At the prices, worth an each-way punt.

Had been going the right way earlier this year with two wins, including a tidy effort at Southwell. Last run was a bit underwhelming, but it came after a short break and she’s capable of better here. If she’s sharper now, she could sneak into the frame. EW chance if bouncing back.

The 9-year-old Under Curfew certainly has had a busy career with 91 runs so far. Stats show 9 wins (7 on turf) and 27 places (16 on turf). His Brighton stats over the years show four 3rd places from just five runs, with the last 3rd being over 5.3f where he was found short of room and keeping on. That was just his third outing on turf since last September following 15 consecutive AW runs. The trainer has been in fair form recently with 5 wins and 8 places from his last 40 runners, whilst 7lb claimer M L Slayter has ridden 6 places from 19 in his short career. Could be thereabouts.

Twirler was 4th over course and distance 10 days ago. Drops 1lb for that and Nicola Currie on board looks an interesting move. Rode a 40/1 2nd for the stable last week. Decent stall draw in 1 and goes on most ground. Solid each way chance here.
Kranjcar is very in and out, but with Billy Loughnane on, this is likely a pretty good bet in this race.

The 6yo mare is in good shape. Three turf runs this year, a little unlucky in running in the first two of those races before a C/D win in a classified stakes last week, a shade cozy in the end by 1L+ - good RPR rating posted. Now running in handicap company but is still on a handy-looking mark.

As adept at the mile or seven furlongs, it’s a bit of a worry that he finished a running-on third to River Wharfe two runs ago over the longer trip and now has to overturn a length and a half defeat with shorter to do so. But he’s been running well enough to think if a bit more use of him is made here, he could do that. Slightly slowly away on that occasion, that allowed the horses flanking him from the gates a bit of a start, and they inconvenienced him straight away. Then on the bends, it was a similar story, and he never really got a clear run, losing a couple of lengths on River Wharfe just around one corner. Under the more experienced (and talented) David Egan, who is 7-41, 17% SR for the yard, I’d like to see him midfield with a bit less work to do at the finish, and there’s no doubting this horse still has a win in him.

A winner over a mile here and making her Brighton 7 furlong debut but is 4 times a winner over this trip on tapeta. Her last 3 runs have all been over a mile here, winning in April, runner-up 17 days later and losing third close to home on the 21st of May. Could welcome the drop in trip here.

River Wharfe also looks like a strong contender in this race. He drops back to 7f after narrowly winning over 8f last time. Goes well fresh and on good to firm ground. Handled by Tony Carroll, Brighton's leading handler. If settling better early, can stalk the pace and finish strong.

Not shown that much in their 3 runs since joining this stable, but is a course winner who is very well handicapped here off dropping mark of 53. Very good/under used jockey booked and in hands of a shrewd upcoming trainer, making current 16/1 decent Ew value here.

ROMAN EMPEROR doesn't find winning that easy but has been steadily improving and stayed on as if he could handle the extra distance last time out. Now drops further in the weights and with two longshots likely to make the running there will be a pace to aim at. This one could be one of the ones that reels them in.

Tony Barron's 4yo gelding is not an obvious selection. This son of Kodiac is a 12-race maiden who beat just five rivals home in his last five starts, so doesn't spring to mind as a horse to follow. But, he's shown some flashes of ability, mainly on the strength of an eye-catching run in a 6f nursery at Southwell in December 2023. Despite going close a couple of times, he generally disappointed, and eight runs later he dropped to a rating of 46. Now down a further 2lbs to 44, I am pleased to see this run is over 7 furlongs as I believe it will suit him better than six. Tony Carroll does well with horses returning from a break and at this track. I hope there may have been a few tweaks since he was last seen. Taking a shot at a big price in what is a weak race.

Noble Guest, a 3??'year??'old Mohaather gelding trained by George Margarson, takes his place in the 7f 216y Star Sports Handicap tomorrow at Brighton with David Egan booked to ride??'a strong booking given Egan’s solid current season form .
He arrives off a career-best second at Lingfield on 31 May, finishing just 2¼ lengths behind over 7f 135y, showing marked improvement and winning a photo-finish contest . Prior runs include creditable efforts at Kempton and Newmarket in mid-May, where he raced with intent on good to firm ground .
With Brighton’s undulating mile-uphill finish this seems a suitable test for his staying qualities, and Egan’s tactical nous may help unlock further progress.
The 5yo is a previous C/D winner. Two runs this year and his fitness should be fine now. He was a close runner-up 10 days ago, having the measure of the rest. He was rated 8lb higher last summer.

Came to hold every chance over 1f out Lto over 1.2 miles @ Yarmouth in similar class race, but did not last home. Won over today's C/D on prior run in a class 6, so drop back to this mile looks a big plus, very good jockey who was on board that day back up and very shrewd trainer has a very impressive 42 percent strike rate with his horses here last 5 seasons, making current 7/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Only beaten by a neck over today's course and distance last time out. Looks capable of going one better here, running off the same mark today.
Cuban Girl or Buy The Dip are my shortlist in this race, but I'm favoring the former in this one. Remains with top connections despite a relatively low mark. Lightly raced and open to progress.

Was well beaten over 1m 2f here in April when returning from six months off but improved to finish runner up over C&D seventeen days later before finishing third over C&D last month. Is a previous course winner over 1m 2f. Should be thereabouts.
Fascinating Lips' record at Brighton isn't anything to write about, but he gets a very tentative vote purely for the reason of being top-rated on both TS and RPR.

Brighton specialist with a 13% chance per statistical projections . Held up and blocked last time at Lingfield, now dropping in grade on a sharp, well-undulating Brighton course. Strong each-way contender based on form and track suitability

Been way below par in recent outings, but has a win, so is capable albeit 50/1 that time. Billy Loughnane can easily get a tune out of Jupiter, and this fella has a squeak at a double-figure price. Could place or better.

Was a winner in their native France for A. Fabre was not not disgraced in a couple of listed/group class races. Has shown nothing since joining this stable via J. Osbourne on Aw/Turf. However, those runs were between 6/8f and selection has a large stamina dosage in nice pedigree, so step up to this 1.4 miles more in line with that breeding. Is incredibly well handicapped in this class 6 classified stakes off lowly mark of 49, also interesting that today's very under used jockey does well when riding for this stable and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 16/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Trainer James Owen has worked his magic on Shadows In The Sky since he got him at the start of this season, finishing 122. With conditions in his favor, this looks like a good opportunity for the 9-year-old gelding.

The model I run suggests She Has Notions can cause an upset and win this one. This model result has been driven by She Has Notions lining up with a comparably high RPR but an official rank that's the joint lowest. This subsequently means less weight is being carried over this longer 3m stamina test. She Has Notions carries an initial weight that is just shy of a 2 stone difference to the top weight and market leaders. Freddie Keighly on board relieves a further 10 lbs as a claiming jockey, and that takes the total weight differential to over 2 and a half stone. That is a significant amount over a 3 miles trip. Tries cheekpieces for the first time, and if all clicks, surely the weight difference will be the main story by the finish line.

Good stable, twice a winner during the winter. Third in its last 3 runs, including last time out under today's jockey, Brian Hughes. Beaten 3 lengths by Stumps or Slips, recorded an RPR of 96. Serious chance.
French Symphony brings untapped potential over fences, switching to chasing for the first time after showing decent form over hurdles, including placing at this course and distance.

Front runner who has two wins and a second at around this distance. Beaten by 'We Got Your Back' over 2m 4f last time out, but this horse is better at the shorter distance. Jockey claims 3lb, whereas 'We Got Your Back' is raised 1lb.
Flash In The Park ran well in April at Warwick. Poor next time, but this is a weak-looking race and is now tried with a tongue tie back on, so expect improvement.

With trainer Mickey Bowen having a 2 week strike rate of 30% and jockey Sean Bowen a 24% strike rate it's fair to say they are both in fantastic form. Karavomylos makes chase debut today after some fair form over hurdles and managed 2 wins at class 4 level. Should be competitive here.

Cave Article won in April at Hereford and in December at Sedgefield so it's two wins in five races. Trainer Christian Williams has a good record in this race and I do think Cave Article will win the first at Southwell today.
Ran in snatches when last seen. Hoping that wind surgery for this horse really works the trick here and can capitalise off this mark
I can't believe the price of this mare. She showed great tenacity last time to regain the lead and go away when headed at this course. Looks great value.

The model I run suggests an outside chance for Fast Deal at 51s is the value bet. This result has been driven by Fast Deal having the highest RPR of the smaller 6 horse race and is very kindly treated in the weights. 2 stone weight difference to the top weight and varying degrees in between around this 3m opener. The reason for the big price is clearly the inconsistency of form and has been pulled up in 3 of the last 6 runs. Surely this risk has to be priced in at 51s. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
Has been running well on the all-weather all winter, and this is a fair mark to start handicapping over hurdles with. Has the most potential here to improve against his mark and should go close.

I'm going against the favorite Carlton here with Lolaos Du Mou. Carlton is going over hurdles handicapping now and might suddenly become a different beast and bring some of his magnificent AW form with him, but I'm hoping he won't. So Lolaos Du Mou is preferred now with the hood going on again. Won a very good race last time out at Warwick on the 21st of May. Tabitha Worsley rides again.

A tight, small affair in which Brindley is given yet another chance under B. Hughes to get off the mark. A run at Newbury a few outings back was his best but he got worn out at the line. Last time out was a 3rd of 6 result when running here at Southwell for the first time.
Back in a maiden hurdle after running in a Class 1 novice. Looks a leading contender in this much weaker race. Runner-up in three similar races, gets 7lb from main rivals.
Ilestdancingspirit has had two respectable runs, both in 2nd place, since coming back from a two-year break. He should at least be placed again, provided he does not have to make the running again.

The model I run suggests Banderas can win this one. This result has been driven by Banderas having a comparably high RPR but goes out carrying the same weight as the others. All 9 horses lining up here step out with the same initial amount of weight. Banderas came a decent 3rd last time out only 34 days ago, so comes here in decent form and race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
This could fall to this Henderson newcomer. It will have been well-schooled for hurdles debut. Interesting.This race does lack any depth

Was not suited by drop back to extended 2 miles Lto and better judged on C/D run prior to that, when staying on well to come 3/7 beaten 12.5 lengths in a similar class novice hurdle. Very good jockey/trainer combination makes current 14/1 decent Ew value here.

The Jamie Snowden trained Janworth was 3rd on her bumper debut and was 2nd on her handicap hurdle debut. She was given a time out to mature further. She returned with a win after an 11-month absence at Sedgefield last month. Up 6lbs but with that run under her belt and young apprentice Joe Anderson taking 3lbs off top weight, she shouldn't be far away.

Sits 3 lbs below the mark she defied to win over CD last year. Dropping back down to the correct trip this time.
She's won twice over this CD, with both wins coming in the space of 14 days. Both wins were registered last year when she won off that 3 lbs higher mark. She won comfortably also, proving this mark is well within range for her.
She ran a cracker over CD on her penultimate run, just bumping into a well-handicapped horse in Faded Fantasy. Beaten just 2L by the winner. To be fair, she was giving 7 lbs in weight to the winner.
She ran okay last time out. Perhaps found the trip stretching her. She clearly isn't a 3M horse. She was only beaten 6L back in 4th place. That run should tee her up nicely for this race. This looks a very winnable race for her.
Alan King's horse has improved in the last two races and does look like the one to improve again. It could get that first win after eight attempts.

Sean Bowen gets the ride on Oneforthefairgreen. She has dropped in the handicap to a new low mark of only 72. The last time Sean rode her, she was 2nd of 8 at Leicester last November. She should be at least placed again, wearing a first-time tongue strap.
Lady's Present fell on her first chase effort recently. As long as she's not unduly affected by that, she has every chance dropped back into this sphere.

Should have finished closer last time, having been set too much to do. But that was a promising effort and on stable debut. More to come from her, and she drops another couple of pounds here. Each-way chance.

Ran her best race over hurdles at Catterick two starts ago when 5th of 11 over two miles. Was keeping on late under hands and heels then but didn’t really improve on handicap debut at Kelso last time when going up in trip. Needs to improve on what we’ve seen so far but could reward each-way interest if doing so.

Land Girls Luck was going okay when the saddle slipped last time and pulled up. Previous two runs were good efforts (while still learning) and the form has been well franked. Today's trip looks ideal, and the 6-year-old with rider's claim is on a good mark and gets the ground well.

Lily Pearl ran a respectable first race over course and distance in 4th place considering she was drawn wide in stall 10 and was stuck out wide for most of the race. She is likely to do much better this time from stall 3 and should win.
I'm taking a chance with this filly against the short favorite. The yard is going well, and this one must have thrived as she more than doubled her price from a yearling to a two-year-old.
Making her debut here, but looking at the pedigree, she could be in with a shout as she is a half-sister to a horse that did win over this distance.

Nicely bred filly related to some smart types, including a speedy juvenile winner (Gobi Desert). Hugo Palmer often has his 2-year-olds ready to go first time out, and this one catches the eye on pedigree. EW shot.

Wasn't beaten far on debut when finishing third over 5f at Thirsk in April but was well beaten over the same trip at Carlisle last month. Step up in trip should suit. Should be involved at the finish.

Their Lto run was an improvement on debut and should come on again over this 6f. Good jockey who does well for this stable up and very shrewd trainer who is in top form @ present, would not be known for his 2yo winners, but is 24 percent with a Lsp of 15.65 in that sphere here last 5 seasons, making current 40/1 worth Ew consideration here.
With the forecast as it is, any extra rain will really bring in Lady La Fay to calculations in this small field.

Henrietta Knight is doing well with her horses, and Educator has been rejuvenated by wind surgery after several mediocre runs over hurdles and one on the all-weather. He has won both runs on the flat since the surgery, both times getting up close to home after being held up at the back over this sort of distance. Oisin Orr takes over from Holly Doyle, but the tactics are not likely to change, and in a five-horse race, traffic problems are not likely at Pontefract.

Knightswood is a proven performer at this distance (26.67% win rate), showing that today’s trip brings out the best in him. His victory at Ripon three starts ago, where he won by a head off a mark of 82, highlights his ability to win in competitive handicaps.

Didn't fire at Hamilton last time, but that was over a longer trip, and he's now back on a mark he can do damage from. Has hinted at better to come earlier this year, and this drop in distance could help. Each-way shout if bouncing back.

Good stable. Tailed off in a handicap hurdle before winning its next two hurdle races. Back on the flat last time out at Nottingham, destroyed the field when beating Fashionelle by 10 lengths. Up 11lb, but that does not look like stopping another win.

Not the easiest to win with, but kept on steadily at Catterick last time over nearly 2 miles. Potter is a reliable type at this sort of distance, and this will suit him. Each-way claims if he is in the mood.

Triple Nickle won off 47 at Ffos Las last summer and followed up with a couple of 3rds off 49, so the form is reliable. She tried hurdles over the winter and a prep run on the AW last time, all without success. She is back on turf today and back on a mark of 47 and should make a place at least.

Was a winner on the flat over 1.6 miles for previous trainer R. Spencer and over 2 miles in the hurdling sphere for current stable. May have found 1.6 miles @ Carlisle on the short side Lto, good apprentice retains ride taking off 3lb and very shrewd dual trainer has a good record in this race, making current 20/1 decent Ew value here.

DIFFERENT DRUM has done much of his running on the all-weather of late but returns to the handicap from a potentially tempting mark here. Forgive the last time out run due to it being the first back from a break. Hopefully, that has served as a tune-up and he's dropped in grade now, so he could get involved.

Yakhabar seems well overpriced here, and I can see this shortening to single odds by tomorrow's off. The good to soft ground will suit, and the increase in distance from his previous race will also help. Runs here on a very low handicap mark.

Finished 2nd here in class 4 over CD 17 days ago beaten 0.75L . Prior to that won class 5 at Beverley over 5f on good to firm . Drops back into class 5 today with claimer taking 3Lb off , yard have won last 2 renewals of this race .

Just caught on the line last time off of 74. One pound higher for that, but with a 7-pound claimer on board, looks well in this sort of company. Solid performance in a Grade 2 handicap at Chester recently, and this looks a much easier task.
No comment made

Ancient Times is an experienced handicapper with a solid record at this class level (4 wins from 11 starts, 36.36% strike rate), suggesting he’s well capable of competing at this grade. He arrives in excellent recent form, with two wins in his last three starts.
Runs here for the first time at mark 58 with a 3lb claiming jockey. With conditions to suit, last win at a mark of 70, certainly has each way claims today.

A 4 year old, he has finished in the first three 6 times from 13 starts on turf, and was last seen finishing 2nd of 5 over 10 furlongs at Beverley in May, with the winner and 3rd subsequently winning. Regular jockey Joanna Mason is in good form as is Trainer Michael Easterby.

Evelyn's Phoenix produced an improved performance last time out at Redcar after a much-needed reappearance at Beverley and can build on that effort now he's back to his last winning mark. A three-time winner last season, including over this distance, he won’t mind some juice in the ground. Breaking from stall 5, David Allan should be able to secure a prominent position, if not make the running, and he looks a contender in this grade. An each-way shout at around 15/2.
Toronto Raptor was unlucky last time when squeezed out while making his move. Last summer he managed a 2nd here off 65. Today, he races off 55 and looks nailed on for a place at least.

The 6yo should be better for his return run two weeks ago, on fast ground and the majority of his rivals were rated 85+ and now facing rivals rated 65-75. He ran to a decent level in his final two starts last year, on slower ground, in class 3 and 2 handicap races while racing off an 8lb higher mark. He can be a big player at this class 5 level on easier ground.

This three time course and distance winner looks good tonight. He wore a visor for the first time last time at Carlisle and responded well to it. So now back at his favourite stomping ground, a good run can be expected.

Won well last time out and although he'll need to find a bit more improvement today, he usually follows up 1 good run with another so he's worth a look again today. This race doesn't look much tougher than his last.

Despite his age, Danzan has proved he retains his ability and looks a contender now dropping in grade, currently ten pounds below his last winning mark. A course and distance winner, he's drawn alongside several slow starters, so I’d expect him to lead or, at worst, secure a good early position, something that could prove crucial. He travelled well for a long way in both starts this term and has been dropped a further 2lb, so he looks a solid each-way player at around 7/1.
Minnesota Lad does look to have an interesting profile here, and Tom Eaves is a good booking for this stable, in my opinion. Better chance than odds suggest.
Was well beaten over 7f at Ayr at the end of April when returning from six months off. Should be fitter today. Is a two time C&D winner. Billy Garrity in good form recently. Should be thereabouts.

Just one win from 10 runs to date. So far this year, things are not going to plan, but only 2 runs this year and a better effort LTO at Nottingham last month. It should have a better chance with a dropped mark and drop down in class.
This looks like another of those runners having had 3 outings without showing much. Now handicapping and over the correct distance, we should see some improvement this evening.

Three runs for the 8yo mare this year and is in decent shape. She was a close 3rd of 12 two starts back. She saw the race out nicely last time out, never landing a blow but she met plenty of traffic problems in the final 2f. On a handy mark now, suited by the track and these lower rated rivals don’t look strong.

Highwaygrey loves it here at the track. He's now 9 and could be on the downgrade, but he's worth an interest now down to a class 6, 3 lbs lower than his last winning mark and returned to a track he loves.
Torn between two horses here. Believe ran a solid third at Hamilton over 8f despite a slow start. Stepping up in trip today, which will suit him, and he is within a good each-way shot here.

Ridden cold in a field of 4 last time at Pontefract, it just didn't really suit this horse. But now with a bigger field, it could get the cover needed, and with Paul Mulrennan keeping the ride, this must remain a good chance.

Khangai, a 5-year-old gelding by Twilight Son trained by James Owen, tackles the Racing For Everyone Handicap over 1m 2f on tomorrow’s Pontefract card. He’ll be ridden by Kaiya Fraser, whose lightweight claim should help his chances in this big-field event .
Khangai arrives off a solid campaign that includes a smooth victory at Chepstow in June 2023 and consistent midfield efforts throughout this season. He’s finished fourth at Bath (building speed early) and sixth at Brighton on good-firm ground??'comfortably handling the rise in class .
His rating of 56 reflects that he’s not outclassed today, and with Fraser aboard to help conserve his stamina early, he could very well sneak into the places. This trip suits his staying ability, and his strong form profile highlights a horse ready for a big run.

Mcted won off 57 and 60 on the turf last year. He switched to the AW over the winter and showed nothing and was unfancied. The lack of a prep run is a concern, but if fit enough, he can win today off 58.
Curious Mrs Fox is worth one more chance off 45. She was a shade unlucky last time and, if she can reproduce her 3rd off 49 this time last year, she might just run into a place today.

Won both times here back in October, and returns here at a similar weight and a nice lower draw. Hasn't won at this distance yet, but has placed 2nd three times. Showed improvement at recent Redcar since returning from a break.
Three runs this year for a new yard, not doing a lot wrong in class 4 and 3 handicap races. More suitable going conditions now for the 4yo, dropping down to class 5 company and down to a handy mark.
Won over course and distance last August from a 3lb higher mark and has been ridden as if she has been building up to something. Drops in class here into a Class 5. NAP BET.

Fierce looks as though he is very much going under the radar here. Has produced some very good efforts over 5 furlongs but, although this 6 furlongs trip is quite stiff, the horse may still be improving and has experience of the distance.

Won at Hamilton in May, and then used up too much energy early on when stepped up to seven furlongs at Redcar last time. Drops back to six furlongs today in a slightly higher grade, but receives weight from all of his rivals and can make that tell. He has only had seven races and surely more improvement to come.

Still 4lb higher than its last win, which came under the same jockey, but did manage a close 2nd off this rating subsequent to that win. I don't think it has run at this course before, but the inclination is to disregard the last run and hope a win is possible off this higher rating.
Not often seen in this class of race and at these very generous odds, and remaining unexposed, I Need Your Love will have a better chance than the odds suggest.
Came a good 3rd 14 days ago over this course and distance and has been dropped 1 lb in the handicap, so sure to have a chance here.
A winner three days ago and looks set to follow up. Was a bit keen over that 6f so the faster pace of 5f today should help. The penalty is unlikely to halt progress.

The 7-year-old is in decent shape. Three turf runs this year, a close runner-up on his return. He was beaten 2 lengths 10 days ago. However, entering the final 2 furlongs, he had no room, and the jockey virtually had to stop riding all the way to the line but was still close up at the finish. Good jockey booking for this apprentice riders’ handicap, and he can still claim a useful 7lb.

There are only 7 runners here, so my e/w tip has to come first or second. I believe we have a chance. Cabeza De Llave has won here in the past and has had 3 runs to get fit. Would like a firmer surface but is in with a chance.

EXQUISEMENT has dropped a stone down the weights for three runs in May and has an apprentice taking a further 3lb off. Looks worth chancing at the 66/1 odds currently available with 3 places on offer in this 7-runner race now dropped to 5f.

Top stable. Ran well on its 2-year-old debut last July, finished 2nd in a Class 2 at Ascot, beaten 1.75 lengths by Tiger Mask. Showed he had trained on when reappearing in May, finishing 2nd at Newbury, beaten 2 lengths by Raafedd, recording an RPR of 84. Cannot oppose.

Twice raced gelded son of Frankel & Emulous ( Dam's sire Dansili ) who represents top connections here looked green in his first career start back on the 20th of September 2024 at Newbury to make any impact whatsoever however he showed the benefit of experience on his second outing when last seen at Kempton 217 days ago finishing a nearest finish 5th/12 and shaped better than that bare result suggest he was still obviously in need of the experience however this is a smart gelding that is likely to rapidly improve and is in top nick for this return to action this is the first time we see him racing as a 3yo and he is much better built and should be a lot more professional over on the business end now as a 3yo and is open to plenty on improvment jockey Rossa Ryan takes the ride and can give R Beckett's inmate the perfect return ride here at Windsor son of Frankel must be taken very seriously on his return to action and is likely to be a whole different proposition this season

Still learning the game after just two starts and didn't build on debut promise when 7th at Southwell last time. That was a muddling race, and he's bred to do better with time and distance. Needs more here, but not one to write off just yet. Each-way possibilities.
Finished a close-up 4th at Newbury on debut over 7f. Was never nearer on that occasion but has scope to improve and is well worth considering.

No show on sole 2yo run, but was only 6/1 in betting market that day, so much better was clearly expected. Decent 3yo comeback when coming 2/4 beaten 2.75 lengths in a similar class maiden over a mile @ Redcar, entitled to come on for that run, under used jockey up and very good training duo 20 percent with their 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.

This J & T Gosden-trained 3-year-old colt went into a few notebooks the way he won on his racecourse debut over one mile one furlong at Wolverhampton. He ran on strongly in the closing stages to beat his more fancied stablemate Cajole by one length. With improvement expected, he should follow up tonight under Oisin Murphy.

Showed big improvement from debut run, when keeping on well over a mile @ Chelmsford Lto to come 4/15 beaten 10.5 lengths in a class 4 maiden. Should relish the 1.2 miles here, good jockey who does well when riding for this stable back up and top class trainer best here with his 3yo's last 5 seasons @ 17 percent, making current 14/1 the Ew play in the race.

With the favorite looking like it only needs to turn up to win, the value is surely each way with this one. It ran an okay race on debut here, and the trainer does well with its 3-year-old runners. At these odds, it looks like very good value.

Gregorian's Star has each-way claims. Winner of a bumper in November 2024 and has shown some ability over hurdles (went quite close to winning at Kempton in April). Slowly away when sixth of eight, beaten 18 lengths at Lingfield in recent novice stakes, but entitled to come on for that run 11 days ago and upped to a more suitable ten furlongs trip this evening. Trevor Whelan takes over the reins for trainer Sheena West.

Change Signs looks an interesting contender in this sprint. While he has only had one go over 5F in 2024 - finishing down the field - it's worth noting he was very keen that day and likely did too much early. His latest run over 6F here was a much stronger effort, just touched off by Circe, going down a short head after leading and only being collared late. Importantly, he pulled nearly 5 lengths clear of the third, suggesting that was solid form. This is further backed up with Circe finishing a decent 5th at Epsom. Before that, he ran a creditable 6th in a competitive York handicap, and earlier in the year he finished a good 3rd behind Habooba at Kempton. That form has worked out nicely, with Habooba going on to win a decent handicap at York and Epsom 5F winner in behind that day (JM Jungle). He is fairly consistent overall and doesn't seem ground dependent. With dry conditions forecast, the going should suit. Drawn in stall 9, which isn't ideal on paper, but he showed good gate speed from stall 13 last time, so that shouldn't be a major concern if he breaks well again.

The last three races that Regal Envoy has raced in, he has always been partnered by Oisin Murphy. Together, they won two and finished second. One of those wins was over today's course and distance. He has gone up three pounds since his latest win, but with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, he is likely to once again steer Regal Envoy to victory.

More than decent Ex Irish performer, who has had 2 runs since joining this stable in Grp class races in Meydan. Going to find this class 2 handicap a lot easier than many of their recent assignments, top jockey up and very shrewd trainer has alway excelled in the sprinting sphere, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Handicap debut for Miraculous. This looks to be a relatively exposed group of horses. If any sort of upside, this looks like a workable mark and can win here.

I can’t be having Regal Envoy or Change Sings here; the former has to shoulder W Knight’s 9% SR (A/E 0.44) with fancied runners when the jockey has 5 mounts that day, meanwhile E Johnson Houghton doesn’t produce decent 5f sprinters (12% SR, A/E 0.46 when fancied). Handicap debutant Miraculous has it all to do off a mark of 99 IMO and I’m not convinced that Miss Attitude is up to winning at this level on evidence of her previous starts. I think an each way play is the way and the one that catches my eye the most is ROSARIO at 14/1. The son of Harry Angel comes out top + blue FlatStats rated and is a consistent sort, winning on his penultimate start at Goodwood. He only beat one home over 6f LTO at Newbury but still only lost by 3.75l and is back down to his preferred 5f today off an unchanged mark. The R Teal yard are having a fantastic season so far (23% SR, A/E 1.85), you’ve got to pay attention when they book C Fallon (22% SR, A/E 1.65) and Teal’s 28% SR (A/E 2.12) with 5f sprinters in C1-3 races adds further confidence.

Woolhampton is a course and distance winner. Was 5th over course and distance 21 days ago and is dropped 1 lb for that effort. On a good mark and is versatile on any ground, so should be capable of a good run here.
Adrestia has won two races at 5f. Fifth over 6f at Chester on her latest outing in August last year. Dropped in trip to 5f should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Miss Attitude, a 5-year-old Cityscape mare trained by Jack Channon, lines up in tomorrow’s 6f 21y Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap at Windsor. Notably, David Probert, in strong form this season, takes the ride??'a confident booking that suggests she’ll be ridden with intent.
Her recent outing at York (May 31) saw her finish a solid fifth of 13 in the William Hill Top Prices Handicap over 5f, staying on well in midfield on good ground. Prior to that, she claimed victory at Southwell on March 4 and ran commendably through the summer of 2024, including a win at Haydock and placed efforts at Goodwood and Doncaster.
Stepping up to Windsor’s extra 21 yards and with Probert’s tactical nous onboard, Miss Attitude looks primed to target the places in a field suited to her sprinting pedigree. She’s one of those proven types who can surprise at decent quotes when conditions click.

A horse with loads of speed who just appears to love running fast. Big improver last year, winning 3 times, but still looked a little green in my opinion. It would seem they just let him run, trying to hold him back a little, like on his seasonal debut where he pulled hard and ran out of steam. But that was a Group 2 and a bit optimistic, and it was his first run. Even this class 2 might prove tough, but I'm willing to give him a shot because he didn't seem the finished article last year, in my opinion, and could have improved again.

Good stable. Four good runs since upped in trip and handicapping, winning twice and placed twice. Last time out stayed on well to beat Glitter Code at Nottingham, recorded an RPR of 69. Another step up in trip can bring about more improvement. The one to beat.

Five career runs for the 3yo filly. She won on her handicap debut during April. Only beaten a head two weeks ago, well clear of the rest. Didn’t have a clear passage - good rating posted. This handicap is not as strong, open to more improvement. Strong jockey change.
Girls Night Out has been well backed here. Still, Aaiden is making a handicap debut, unexposed, and a lot better is expected here than bare form.

Gelded son of Ardad who was last seen at Haydock 17 days ago where finishing 5th/8 however his mark continues to ease and he is now operating on a mark 61 and he can begin to trouble the judge also stepping up in trip tackling the 1 mile 2 furlong trip for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this trip can unlock a whole new level of improvment and seeing he is on a handy mark in a suitable looking assignment I Furtado's inmate must enter calculations jockey S De Sousa takes the ride and can give Space Raider a promising ride here at Windsor

Having raced 3 times, this maiden finished 3rd in a Novice race at Lingfield 42 days ago. She is now making her handicap debut and has the potential to improve. An each-way bet at 25/1 is well worth considering.
Dictal's pedigree jumps off the page and seems to have the best chance in this field. Promising support in the market on first start too.
Promising debut 3rd in a Haydock maiden and only beaten a neck for second. Showed plenty of pace that day and can make all today.
Well-bred Supremacy filly who cost 50,000 guineas as a yearling. Related to winners, and her dam scored in the US over 8.5f as a juvenile. Looks good on pedigree and worth an each-way chance here.
Gained valuable experience in debut run over C&D when a credible 4th of 14 earlier this month. So will be looking for some improvements, which just might be enough to win this one.

Ran much better than form figure would indicate on debut run, as nothing went right for them. Dwelt @ start, got badly outpaced, was making good headway final furlong when getting hampered, before keeping on well to come 3/7 beaten 5.25 lengths in a class 5 maiden over 6f on Aw @ Kempton. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, good jockey retains ride and very good trainer who is in form, tops here numerically last 5 seasons, making current 14/1 solid Ew value in the race.

This is a hot 2yo race which the Frankel favorite will win. I have a 28/1 shot to get a place, Miss Kim by Palace Pier, £32,000 covering fee. Siblings have made a good start to the season: 5 runs, 2 wins, 2 places. We were in front backing these. The trainer has had a newcomer win lately, so looking good. E/W nap 28/1.

An Oasis Dream filly, a half-sister to the 5f winner Sudden Flight. Her dam was a 6f winner. Trainer Richard Hughes is currently in excellent form and has a strong track record with debutants. The odds of 40/1 present a valuable opportunity for an each-way bet, especially with the added advantage of the jockey's 5lb claim.
Boy George looks a solid enough bet here. He has been running well of late, and this race looks ideal for him to get another win for an in-form trainer and yard.

8-year-old who has hit good form, winning the last two starts and goes up 4lb for the latest win. But won with a bit in hand, so could land the hat-trick. Good apprentice keeps the ride and claims 7lb.

Showed a bit of spark in blinkers last season, finishing placed twice, but couldn't match that form in cheekpieces on stable debut for Jim Boyle. Blinkers go back on now, which may help rekindle some of that earlier promise and definitely not dismissed for a place here.
Has been hovering in and around this mark for quite a while and pops up semi-regularly with a win. Could be a very good chance here after a bit of a dry spell.

Moonlit Cloud won off 70 at Bath a year ago and was raised 5lb for that which proved too much. She has had a prep run on the AW and runs well when back on turf after an AW run. She runs today off 65 and should go close off that mark.
Lawn Ranger is another big price possibility here, has been running well of late and shown glimpses of promise in a number of runs for Michael Attwater.
Disappointed last time out when eighth, but fifth at Chelmsford before that is comparable to anything else in this race, so is given the verdict at a decent price.
Magical Idea has got a very nice page, and although didn't do that well on the first start, can improve here for a yard that usually needs a first run under their belts.

Clear signs of inexperience but the performance wasn’t devoid of promise despite finishing 7th of the 10 runners over an extended mile at Leicester. This looks like a similar race and although likely to be sent off at massive odds could outrun those and sneak into the frame.

No show on sole 3yo run, but 4yo return was a bit better than it looks on paper and entitled to come on for that run. Should appreciate the mile today on nice pedigree, dropping in grade here, very under used jockey retains ride and very good trainer 29 percent with his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 50/1 decent Ew value in the race.
Best form of these over hurdles, having finished 3rd in the Dawn Run last year, and has the best form of these over fences, where she is likely to be a better chaser. The one to be on here.

Runcok switches to chasing after a poor run last time over hurdles. But he was highest rated over hurdles, and if he jumps well enough on his first attempt over fences, he should beat the more experienced mare Birdie Or Bust, who gained her first win last time helped by the fall of challenging Out For A Stroll two out at Killarney. She made all there over further.

The model I run suggests Encanto Bruno can win this one. Encanto Bruno lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the rest of the field but is not overly penalized for it in the weights. All runners go out with a very similar weight to carry around this 2m round trip. Encanto Bruno is one of the few showing form coming into this contest. A decent second 57 days ago and is a previous distance winner, so knows how to get the job done at this distance. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Zenta was a Grade 1 winner over hurdles and won a mares' beginners chase in February, beating her more fancied stablemate Pagane into 3rd place. She could be a danger to Pied Piper, getting eleven pounds not including her rider's three pounds allowance, but she has to bounce back from being pulled up in a Listed handicap chase last month.
Class hurdler taken well to chasing. Won its last 2 races by over 20 lengths. Looks nailed on here. Ground and trip will suit.

Boston Rover was progressive but remained a maiden over hurdles. He could have needed his first run over fences after a break of 158 days when finishing 2nd at Limerick, where he made a few mistakes, including at the last, after making a lot of the running.

Reserve here, so would need one to drop out, but good price at 16-1. Good trainer, obviously, in Gavin Cromwell. 7lbs claimer up. Two wins from eight over hurdles and has had more experience than many over fences. Started favourite for a handicap chase at Down Royal in December and ran second there. Never really got involved on return at Killarney last month. Useful 7lbs claim by virtue of being a mare. By Jukebox Jury. Possible.

Has been running well in defeat of late @ this level and retains a decent mark of 110 here. Good conditional back up claiming 5lb and in hands of a very shrewd trainer, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Finished lame when fifth last May 24 in a chase and has been kept off the track since, so fitness is taken on trust. But looks a potential improver in this sphere, and the leading owner keeps this 9-year-old. Has won over hurdles, so has ability in this grade.

Ran well in defeat last time out, that was his first start over fences where he left the impression he'll be winning some races over fences at some point, races such as this race. Likely to be wiser with that experience so could improve on that last run. This horse does have some good hurdles form, if he can transfer that hurdles form to fences , he'll be doing well. This horse is one of a few who is likely to improve over fences.

Presenting Max is a fair hurdler who stepped up to a chase run with a solid 3rd of 11 in the handicap at Kilbeggan 45 days ago. He showed a fair amount of ability over the fences and should be competitive again here for an EW place or better.

A fall early on chase debut at Killbeggan scuppered the chance of Lehaunstown. He's quickly returned to the track seemingly none the worse for the fall. Connections are obviously keen to get him started over fences and they have a good record at this venue.

Inthenickoftime is a 5-year-old gelding trained by E Bolger. He is a hurdles winner who has taken well to chasing, finishing third in his first two starts. He posted a career-high RPR of 100 when finishing 3/15 last time out behind two decent yardsticks. He should be considered on his second start in a handicap chase under Kevin Sexton.

Andyourbirdcansing has only completed once in her last four races, so her jumping is a problem. Her latest was an unseat over hurdles, but over the minimum distance, she could make the running and go close with a clear round off her lowly mark of 90.

Prince Of Air appears as one of the more interesting contenders, arrives with some of the best recent form and considering that he's been fairly lightly raced of late , it's possible he can take a step forward today.

Finished tenth of 11 in a handicap chase at Kilbeggan over nearly 20f, 45 days ago. The booking of Millar adds some weight here for a better ride, and the form suggests he remains competitive. Worth a small win bet today if the ground conditions suit him.

BALTINGLASS HILL is not fully exposed as a handicap chaser and jockey Dylan Robinson has ridden this eight year old previously. Well treated for racing in this sphere and no doubt the Philip Rothwell trained runners are moving much better now. One at decent odds worth considering.

My EW choice here. Pahlavi ran a not too bad 7th of 11 in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel over 17f about 53 days ago. Now makes his chase debut and steps into handicap chase company for the very first time. Could improve with the switch to fences if he transfers the ability and worth a small EW shot at good odds.

This horse appeared to find the 2m 6f trip just a bit too far last time out, did get outpaced on more than one occasion , this drop in trip will suit better , might be worth one more chance. Has shown enough overall to think this horse is in with a small each-way chance.

Dreamz is making her chase debut, and while this mare will need to jump better than some of her efforts over hurdles, she should be suited by the good ground. Her best form in bumpers and over hurdles would see her go close if she takes well to the bigger obstacles.

Willie Mullins has the front two in the betting here with Luckinthecity and Uncle Pat, both on chase debut. But Uncle Pat is coming off a 260-day break since winning over hurdles at Listowel, and Luckinthecity may be the more race-fit for his first chase.

A useful hurdler on his day, he made a promising debut over fences in a three-mile novice at Tipperary, finishing the race off well. His jumping was pretty good and he is likely to be suited by this slightly longer trip. Unlikely to be far away.
Males Chase debut. Always been thought of as a future chaser, and though he will probably come on for the run, Mullins is more than capable of having one ready first time up.

Barry Connell is one of the best at training his horses to change codes - chasing to hurdling or vice versa. Slane Hill made the perfect start to his chasing career 2 years ago when winning his beginner's chase. He has not kicked on but has been over timber for the last year or so. Now, up in trip and back over fences, if he can limit the mistakes and on his preferred good ground, he can go well under Walsh, who has done well in these rider-limited races with two wins.

Down another 2 pounds today and is currently 3rd favorite. Brazil hasn't won since 2022 and has had another 12 runs since. Recently finished below-par 7 of 14 in a handicap chase at Killarney over 26f, but the way he ran was in pockets of good and bad. So with a better ride today and lower weight, he could actually win and regain his form.

The model I run suggests Doran's Law can cause an upset and win this one. Doran's Law is not too fancied by the early market. This model result has been driven by Doran's Law having an RPR comparable to the rest of the field but an official ranking leaving it very well treated at this mark. Goes out carrying the second lowest weight over this longer 3m 1f stamina test with 15 runners. A good second-place finish 35 days ago and looks to build on that here today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Back down to same mark as when winning at Punchestown in May last year. Has been nowhere near that form in three races this year but has shown gradual improvement, and if settling better than he did at Killarney last month, he could easily take a hand in the finish.

Arrycan is open to some improvement this year, today is just his 2nd run back from a rest. That was a very good run when finishing 2nd of 12 over 3m 2f last time out, the slight drop in trip today may be more suitable. This horse does have very good form in the book at this course so he's difficult to overlook in what looks like an open race.

Mica Malpic was coming off a 529 day break when 7th and well beaten at Tipperary last month over 2m 1f but he did not get a clear run and was not knocked about after his chance had gone. He should appreciate the step up in distance.

AMBITIOUS FELLOW may have been geared up for this specific race as a spring/summer target. He had ace conditional jockey Jake Coen aboard latest retaining the ride and he is well treated as a chaser given his significantly higher hurdles mark. Ground-versatile and a lively outsider.

Hascoeur Clermont has got to be worth a small e/w wager at 66/1 just because he has finished 2nd twice over CD, including this race last year when rated 123. Down to 120 today with the same ground conditions, the trainer's last two runners have finished 2nd and 3rd, so the stable may be beginning to fire now. This horse likes to be up with the pace, so this could be a nice little lay in play to recoup your stake during the race. You should be able to lay at least half these odds for a free bet and still have a 33/1 runner in play. Worth thinking about.

This year’s Connacht National looks intriguing, especially with the rain expected to hit the turf in County Roscommon tomorrow. One horse I’m keen to back is Eric McNamara’s 11-year-old veteran, DONKEY YEARS. While he wasn’t terrible in the competitive Killarney National last month, he plugged on steadily over 26f. This son of ROBIN DES CHAMPS drops 1lb for that effort and gets a further 5lb relief thanks to jockey Gary Noonan, who has been in solid form with a 20% place strike rate over the past month. Noonan also boasts a respectable 36.36% place strike rate over the past five years at this track. McNamara, the trainer, has a 26.09% place strike rate recently.
As mentioned, the expected rain should suit this old boy down to the ground, with his best form on ground ranging from yielding to downright swampy conditions. The significant drop in class is another positive. This Old Boy is now 6lbs lighter than his last win over fences and, when factoring in the jockey’s claim, he’s on the same winning mark over hurdles. At 16/1, I think he offers a little hope, enough at least to have a little skin in the game.

Only his second start over fences, but I saw enough on his debut. He was jumping well and economically at the rear until jumping too low and upending. But with his good jumping, the ride of Mr. Derek O'Connor, and the increase in trip, it all points towards a positive run.

Cullenwaine has looked back to some better form on his last 2 runs , that was a good 5th over this distance last time out, runs from a 1 lb lower mark today. Today's race doesn't look much tougher than his last. Small each-way tip.

The handicapper isnt doing this veteran any favours but he's been making the frame over shorter trips and should relish this stanina test. Top pilot booked, he should give backers a good run for their money.

The model I run suggests an upset by The Eye of Tulla for the last race of the day. The Eye of Tulla lines up for this larger 16 horse race with the highest RPR of any of the runners here. Has been given an official rating of 75, which is the lowest of all the runners and therefore carries the lowest amount of weight on this 3m 1f stamina test. The claiming jockey, Mr. Nugent, picks up the reins and relieves a further 7 lbs off his back, which is valuable over this sort of distance. Not shown signs of form or fluency, but if getting back to potential, can cause an upset. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

With just one win from 28 National Hunt runs, Max Time makes his chase debut here and is hooded for the first time. Was 11th of 18 in a handicap hurdle at Listowel over 23f, and from watching the replays, he could surprise if adapting well to chasing today. Each Way shot for a place.
Oldtown To Emly won a maiden at Ballingarry on his latest run and gets in here with very little weight off a mark of only 76 based on his hurdle performances in 2023 and 2024.

Brian McMahon's 7-year-old gelding, GREAT RAINBOW, may not look like an obvious candidate on paper, but I’m inclined to give him the benefit of the doubt for his debut over fences 18 days ago at Limerick, especially after a 230-day absence. Pedigree-wise, this son of GREAT PRETENDER should be well-suited to both the tough weather and the staying distance. He looked to be staying on well in similar conditions at Ballinrobe (22f) when last seen on heavy ground.
There are a couple of other positive factors. First, the trainer’s recent form, with an impressive 71.43% place strike rate over the past fortnight, alongside a respectable 26.67% place strike rate here at Roscommon over the last five years. Secondly, while jockey Stephen Connor is still classed as inexperienced, he’s in good form, with a 75% place strike rate over the past month and a perfect 100% place strike rate at Roscommon from his two previous rides.
I wouldn’t rush to the bookies, but I’m happy to have a small tentative poke, Given the conditions, trainer, and jockey form, I think he has a sniff.
Blew the cobwebs away over hurdles last time after 5 months off and now reverts back to fences, having won from just a 3 lb lower mark over fences last October. Decent each-way chance.

Al Arrivee is a 5-year-old daughter of Tunis ex Al Gane from the family of Al Co by Dom Alco. Last time out on her racecourse debut, she was 1 length second at 5/6f in a fillies 4-year-olds only bump behind Rock On By 20/1 by Kayf Tara last October. That bumper has produced two winners from two runners. She moves up in distance here to a 2m2f bumper where she'll again be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins and in the colors of his mother Mrs. J. Mullins. She makes the long journey from her Closutton base and she may be too strong for her rivals here. I make her my Nap of the day.
